To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) smoke emission uncertainties have large effects on simulated smoke loading and radiative effects at local scale, but the effect is much smaller at regional scale, 2) uncertainties in smoke emission inventories are not well constrained and need further improvement, 3) smoke emission uncertainties are likely to be the largest source of uncertainties in smoke-related model simulations, and 4) smoke emission uncertainties need to be further reduced to improve the reliability of model predictions of smoke effects on atmospheric aerosol, air quality
the smoke direct radiative forcing is sensitive to the emission inventory, and that the uncertainty in the smoke direct radiating forcing can be up to 33% at the local scale.
